newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: INTERVIEW-San Teh expands cement business.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-San Teh expands cement business.

text.p: San Teh Ltd plans to raise at least US$20 million in bond or share placements to finance a second cement plant in China, company officials said on Tuesday. The plant, with a capacity of 1.2 million tonnes per year, will transform the rubber keypad maker into an infrastructure-related building materials supplier, they said.
"It is to fund our share of the increase in capital in the cement plant," Lam Ding Ling, group financial controller and also company secretary, told Reuters in a telephone interview.

Fujian Longyan San Teh Cement Buildings Materials Industry Company (FLSC), in which San Teh has a 69.7 percent stake, plans to build a second cement plant in China and needs a US$85 million cash injection.

"San Teh's share is about US$21 million for this," Lam said. The rest would be funded by internal funds and bank borrowings. The other FLSC shareholders are the Chinese government, which owns five percent, and Hong Kong-based San Teh Xing, which is partly owned by San Teh.
According to group chairman Kao Shin Ping, San Teh would buy out the remaining stakes in FLSC if the price is right.
Its intention is to list the cement company by 2000 when it can command a better price-earnings multiple, Kao said.
No decision has been made as to where the company would be listed but Kao said it could be on the New York Stock Exchange.
About 50 percent of group sales, which reached Singapore $82 million last year, would come from FLSC in 2001.
By then, keypad products will account for less than half compared to about 80 percent now, Kao said.
The first plant, with a full capacity of 2,000 tonnes of cement a day, is expected to start operations on May 18.
Output will be about a quarter of a million tonnes this year, Lam said.
"We will target 90 percent capacity next year. That is about 600,000 tonnes a year. From 1999, we will run at full capacity," he said.
The plant is expected to break even early next year and is expected to have sales of US$10 million in 1997 and US$30 million in 1998.
In the beginning, the bulk of the output would be sold into the Chinese domestic market. But the company plans to gradually increase its exports, targetting Taiwan and Southeast Asia, Lam said.
"We can export about 70 percent of our output in 10 years time," he said.
The second plant would be constructed next year and be operational in 2000, bringing total output to 1.8 million tonnes a year with potential sales of about US$90 million.
